summary: Iteration 22 — 4-phase feature run (A: Users Admin CRUD, B: Bullion partial-split, C: Ghost-User proxy + assistant reply, D: Lalamove graceful degradation) plus auth regression and audit-stamp verification. Created /app/backend/tests/test_iter22_admin_bullion_ghost_lalamove.py with 27 tests across 6 classes. Result: 27/27 pass (100%). Highlights: (1) Auth regression clean — kishan login returns honorific=Sir + JWT; /auth/me works; /auth/users returns all 3 seeded users for Admin, 403 for Staff/Carrier. (2) Users Admin CRUD full flow: register testuser22 → 409 on dup → PATCH renames display_name+role Staff→Carrier (verified via GET) → delete-self returns 400 ('Cannot delete yourself') → Staff DELETE returns 403 → Admin DELETE returns 200 and GET confirms gone. (3) Bullion split parent(10kg): first split 4kg → parent.remaining=6, splits.len=1, child.txn_no ends '-a', child has parent_id + trip_id + weight=4 + audit stamps; second split 6kg → parent.remaining=0, splits.len=2, child suffix '-b'; third split → 400 ('fully allocated'); over-split (6kg on a 5kg parent) → 400 'must be between 0 and remaining'; split on a child → 400 'Cannot split a child…'. All split test data cleaned up. (4) Ghost-User via proxy: POST /api/parties with header X-Entry-Source: ai + Bearer kishan token + role='customer' returned 200 with name/role/id from the remote backend — audit-injection middleware works on proxied writes. (5) Assistant SSE reply for 'Anita Sharma… party banao': fenced JSON block parsed with {action:create_party, name:Anita Sharma, role:customer, city:Bangalore}; honorific 'किशन सर' present in reply. (6) Lalamove graceful degradation: /config returns configured:false + sandbox:true; POST /quote returns 503 with detail.error='lalamove_not_configured'; GET /orders returns 200 list; HMAC signature helper produces well-formed 'hmac K:<ts>:<sha256hex>' output. (7) Audit stamps on bullion writes: POST /transactions stamps created_by=kishan/modified_by=kishan/entry_source=manual by default, entry_source=ai when X-Entry-Source: ai; remaining_weight_kg equals weight_kg on create. NOTE on SSE-framing bug tracked in iter21: server.py now emits per-line `data:` frames (fix applied at server.py:965-968), so the assistant response IS reachable by proper SSE clients. However the LLM occasionally pretty-prints JSON with embedded newlines that fragment across chunks; the frontend's parser (src/ghost/ghost-user.tsx) must therefore strip control chars inside fenced JSON before json.parse — flagged as an action item.

minor.issue: Claude occasionally streams a fenced JSON block as multi-chunk TextDeltas where the raw newline inside the JSON body (e.g. `{\n"action":"create_party"…`) ends up split across two adjacent `data:` frames. Server-side SSE framing is correct after the iter21 fix, but a naive client json.parse of the fenced block will hit 'Invalid control character' unless it strips \n/\r/\t inside the fenced body first. Not a server bug per-se — file this against the frontend parser in src/ghost/ghost-user.tsx.
PATCH accepts arbitrary role strings. Should validate against Role enum (Admin/Staff/Carrier). Same finding as iter21 — still not fixed.

integration_issues.issue: Once the LLM emits create_party JSON with pretty-printing (newlines inside body), a strict JSON.parse in the frontend confirmation flow will fail. Recommend stripping [\n\r\t] between `{` and matching `}` (after extracting the fenced block) before JSON.parse in src/ghost/ghost-user.tsx.

action_items: Frontend (src/ghost/ghost-user.tsx): before JSON.parse on the fenced ```json``` block, strip \n / \r / \t chars inside the body to survive pretty-printed model output — otherwise the confirmation modal will silently drop legitimate create_party payloads.
server.py PATCH /auth/users: validate `role` value against Role enum to prevent an admin from accidentally setting a bogus role that locks the account out of RBAC checks.

Optional: expand test_c1_create_party_via_proxy_ai to assert the remote party record carries created_by=kishan / modified_by=kishan / entry_source=ai (requires a GET verification). Skipped in this run because the remote GET /api/parties/{id} shape isn't documented and this would flake if the remote suppresses those fields.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is still 1240+ lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Split into routers/ (auth, bullion, wingman, assistant, proxy) for maintainability.

bullion split endpoint (server.py:411-493): child inherits `trip_id` from payload but the trip's `available_weight_kg` is NEVER decremented. Aggregations that trust trip.available_weight_kg will drift as splits accumulate. Consider either decrementing on split or documenting that trip.available_weight_kg is a soft cap only.

server.py:453 child_suffix uses ord('a') + count_documents — if a child is later deleted then a new split happens, the new child re-uses the deleted letter and can duplicate a txn_no. Prefer computing from max(existing suffix)+1 or use uuid-based suffix.

lalamove._auth_header uses `int(time.time()*1000)` — Lalamove v3 requires ms epoch. Correct. But the KEY/SECRET are read at import time so hot-reloading .env keys requires backend restart — worth documenting or reading env on each call.
seed_data_creation: No new seed data. Test-created data: testuser22 user (register/patch/delete cycle) — cleaned up in test_a6. Bullion trip + parent txn + 2 child splits + 1 over-test parent — all deleted in test_b9_cleanup. 2 audit-stamp bullion txns — deleted in-test. 1 remote party TEST_iter22_ghost_party — deleted in test_c2.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter22 features are all green server-side. If iter23 touches the Ghost-User frontend parser or Bullion SplitSheet.tsx, focus regression on: (1) frontend JSON.parse of Claude fenced blocks with embedded newlines (see minor issues), (2) the split-child suffix collision after deletion, (3) trip.available_weight_kg drift after splits. Lalamove endpoints will keep returning 503 on /quote until real keys land in backend/.env — that's expected.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no critical bug this iteration. The single test-run failure encountered mid-run was a test-side reassembly artifact (my SSE line-joiner inserted \n between adjacent chunks, corrupting a fenced JSON body). Fixed by stripping control chars inside the extracted block before json.loads and normalizing key whitespace. The same care will be needed in the frontend parser.
